evals.prompt: Brief a delegated assignment whose author says its base is already on the integration branch because a two-dot range is empty.
evals.expected_output: Verifies the base claim personally with git merge-base --is-ancestor and counts commits behind the integration head with git rev-list --count; does not infer ancestry from a two-dot range. Writes one self-contained brief with an id, whole task, integration branch, verified base commit, owned files or area, skills, finish line, stop condition, GPU grant and Needs you / Changed / Found report shape. Requires the assignment's last commit to carry Brief: <id> done or Brief: <id> blocked: <question>; treats the message as notification and git as record.

evals.prompt: One batch lands while two local batches remain open. An agent is denied a merge and another reports conflicting generated shader interfaces and fingerprints. How do you proceed?
evals.expected_output: Keeps batch branches local-only in worktrees under .claude/worktrees, cut from the current integration head. Merges the new integration head into every open batch before qualification and routes GPU qualification to verification. The lead runs the denied merge; agents resolve generated-file conflicts with their generators rather than hand-merging. Lands work on the integration branch and moves complete milestones to main only when the owner asks.

evals.prompt: Choose machines for a GPU leg and a heavy build. The GPU machine has more free RAM at this instant than the other machine.
evals.expected_output: Plans by fixed CPU class, GPU, total memory and supported workloads, not fluctuating free-memory or free-disk snapshots. Schedules one GPU leg per GPU and keeps heavy builds off its machine while it runs. Routes grants, GPU work classification and execution to verification.

evals.prompt: The owner asks for more Claude participation while a Sol lane is underway. Choose a family for a new correctness-heavy lane and close a review whose second round still raises a blocker and an out-of-scope finding.
evals.expected_output: Treats steering as an adjustment to judgement, not a quota or a reason to reassign the Sol lane. Chooses Astra or Opus for correctness-heavy work and Sol or Sonnet for well-specified work; uses Fable only when genuinely needed. Routes review with fixes enabled to the writer's other family under review-passes, ending at two rounds. The lead rules on remaining second-round findings with a scoped fix, recorded open item or reasoned dismissal. Gives every finding a lane or named scope deferral before setting it aside.

evals.prompt: Send a partner a long analysis for brief render-batch and proceed if they do not reply.
evals.expected_output: Uses a short message whose self-contained first line is [render-batch] <started|progress|done|blocked|question>: <sentence>. Places the large analysis on a branch and sends its path. Does not treat silence as agreement.
